findings.note: Said at the LWV candidate forum (transcript from On the Record). He is describing a state law that ended the use of a student ID as a voter ID, and says he questioned the bill's author about it. Text taken from the extracted transcript file, since the OTR page loads by script.

findings.passage: One of the saddest things that I see, and it happens every election cycle, if you go to the county election board when they meet about 10 days after the election, they go through their provisional ballots.
findings.note: In the same forum, Pierce describes provisional ballots cast by students who were not registered in the county. The passage is the start of that answer; the next sentence continues in the same answer.

findings.passage: Yeah, I think it's going to take a lot of education, particularly because, you know, over my objections, the Republicans adopted a law which took away the right of the student ID to be used as a voter ID, even though it met every exact. And I made the author of the bill. For like 15 or 20 minutes, I led him through every single aspect of this, and he could not give a good reason why they were doing it. And so that makes it harder to vote. So you've got to educate people about what you need to do to vote.
findings.note: In an On the Record forum transcript (League of Women Voters candidate forum), Pierce says he objected when a law ended the use of student IDs as voter ID, and says that makes voting harder. The transcript is automatic, so some wording is garbled.

findings.passage: Again, as I was saying broadly, it's just this whole basket of issues surrounding preservation of democracy, and that means fighting off voter suppression and these attempts to kind of militarize the law enforcement.
